name: Soup and Stew Week
summary: Big pots that taste even better the next day: red lentil and carrot soup, chicken and white bean stew, beef and barley soup, smoky turkey and black bean soup, salmon chowder and a barley minestrone, with fresh salads and fruit on the side. No bread, rice or pasta.
howItWorks:
**One pot, two meals.** Six dinners make two portions, so each pot feeds the next day's lunch: lentil soup Monday, chicken and white bean stew Tuesday, beef and barley soup Wednesday, turkey and black bean soup Thursday, salmon chowder Friday and minestrone Saturday. Soups taste better after a night in the fridge, and Sunday's fish stew is the only dinner that is fresh and single.

**Fish three times.** Sardines on Monday's lunch and salmon in Friday's chowder (with Saturday's leftovers) bring omega-3 and some **vitamin D**, which is hard to get from food. Sunday's cod stew is a lean third fish. Beans, lentils, chicken, turkey and beef carry the iron, zinc and choline.

**Whole-food carbs only.** Barley, potatoes, sweet potatoes, oats and beans do the work that bread, rice and pasta usually do. Fresh sides and fruit, in the snack slots, add crunch and vitamin C: cucumber salad, veggie sticks with tahini, apples and kiwi. Wash all fruit and vegetables before cutting, lemons too.

**Quick mornings.** Overnight oats and yogurt bowls take five to ten minutes, and the scramble about 15 (8 if you microwave the sweet potato the night before). Eggs appear at three breakfasts (two scrambles and Saturday's hash), always cooked until the yolk is firm.

**What changes with size.** Light keeps the meat, fish and eggs (only the chicken drops a little), trims the oils, nuts, seeds, beans, grains, potatoes and some dairy, drops a snack from Wednesday to Sunday and swaps Thursday's oats for the kiwi bowl. Big grows the portions and swaps Monday's tahini snack for the apple and fennel salad.

recipes.name: Overnight oats with berries and walnuts
recipes.about: Rolled oats soaked in milk and yogurt until creamy, with frozen berries that thaw into a jammy swirl and a crunch of walnuts. Made in five minutes the night before, it brings **fibre, protein and plant omega-3 from the walnuts** before you've touched the stove.
steps: Wash your hands, then stir the oats, milk, yogurt and cinnamon together in a jar until no dry oats are left.
Spoon the frozen berries on top, put the lid on and refrigerate overnight. They thaw and bleed into the oats, which is exactly what you want.
In the morning, stir it up and loosen it with a splash of milk if it is thick. Scatter on the walnuts so they stay crisp.
Keep it in the fridge and eat each jar within 2 days of making it.
recipes.tip: Mix each jar the night before. If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.

recipes.name: Kiwi yogurt bowl with oat crunch
recipes.about: Thick Greek yogurt with sliced kiwi and a warm crunch of toasted oats and walnuts. Kiwi brings **vitamin C**, the yogurt brings protein and calcium, and it takes ten minutes.
steps: Wash the kiwi. Peel and slice it.
Toast the oats and walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they smell nutty, about 3 minutes. Tip them onto a plate to cool for a minute.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl, lay the kiwi on top, and scatter on the warm crunch and the cinnamon.
recipes.tip: Toast a double batch of the crunch and keep it in a jar for the week.

recipes.name: Potato, spinach and pepper hash with firm eggs
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by the diner skillet hash
recipes.about: Crisp-edged diced potato with red pepper and spinach, topped with eggs cooked right in the pan until the yolks are firm. A slow weekend breakfast with **protein, vitamin C and potassium** in one skillet.

ingredients.note: scrubbed and cut into small dice, skin on

steps: Wash the potatoes, pepper and spinach. Cut the potatoes into small dice, about 1 cm, so they cook through quickly.

Warm the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the potatoes, salt and paprika, cover, and cook, stirring now and then, until golden at the edges and tender when poked, about 15 minutes.
Add the onion and pepper and cook until soft, about 4 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, about 1 minute.

Make a well in the hash for each egg and crack them in. Cover and cook until the whites are opaque and the yolks are firm all the way through, 6 to 8 minutes. Break the yolks gently to be sure there is nothing runny.
Finish with black pepper and serve straight from the pan. Wash your hands, the cutting board and the pan after handling raw egg.
recipes.tip: Microwave the diced potato for 3 minutes first and the pan time drops to about 8 minutes.

recipes.name: Spinach and pepper scramble with sweet potato
recipes.about: Firm scrambled eggs with wilted spinach and red pepper, over crisp-edged cubes of sweet potato, with sliced kiwi on the side. The eggs bring **protein and choline**, and the kiwi's vitamin C helps your body absorb the iron in the spinach.

ingredients.note: scrubbed and cut into small dice

steps: Wash the sweet potato, spinach, pepper and kiwi. Dice the sweet potato very small, about 1 cm, so it cooks fast, and dice the pepper. Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper.

Microwave the diced sweet potato with a splash of water for 3 minutes. Warm the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat, add the sweet potato, and cook uncovered, stirring now and then, until browned at the edges, about 5 minutes.
Add the pepper and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, about 30 seconds.
Pour in the eggs and keep folding gently until they are set with no runny egg left, about 2 minutes. They should be firm, not wet, and reach 71 °C (160 °F).
Serve with the sliced kiwi. Wash your hands, the pan and the board after handling raw egg.
recipes.tip: Dice and microwave tomorrow's sweet potato tonight, then cool it and keep it covered in the fridge, and the morning takes about 8 minutes.

recipes.name: Sardine, white bean and spinach salad
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Italian tonno e fagioli, made with sardines
recipes.about: Flaky sardines, creamy white beans, baby spinach and crunchy red pepper in a sharp lemon dressing, a cool fresh plate to start a week of hot pots. The sardines bring **omega-3 fats, vitamin D and soft-bone calcium**.

ingredients.note: very thinly sliced, red if you have it

steps: Wash the spinach, pepper and parsley. Slice the pepper and the onion very thinly.
In a bowl, whisk the lemon juice, olive oil and black pepper. Add the white beans, pepper and onion and toss. Let them sit for 5 minutes so the onion softens a little.
Pile the spinach on a plate, spoon the bean mixture over, and lay the sardines on top. Scatter the parsley over everything.

Eat it right away, or pack the beans and the spinach separately and put it together at lunch. If you pack it, keep the sardines and beans in a cold bag with an ice pack and eat it the same day, within 4 hours.
recipes.tip: Stir the dressed beans into the spinach only at the last minute so the leaves stay crisp.

recipes.name: Red lentil and carrot soup with lemon yogurt
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Middle Eastern shorbat adas
recipes.about: A silky, golden soup of red lentils and sweet carrots, warmed with cumin and turmeric and brightened with lemon. A spoonful of yogurt and toasted sunflower seeds finish it. The lentils bring **iron, folate and fibre**, and the lemon helps your body absorb that iron.
steps: Wash the carrots and parsley. Slice the carrots and dice the onion.

Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrots and cook, stirring, until the onion is soft and golden at the edges, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin and turmeric for 1 minute, until it smells toasty.

Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes and broth, with a splash of water if you need it. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, until the lentils and carrots are completely soft, about 18 minutes.
Blend about half the soup with an immersion blender, or mash it with a potato masher, so it is creamy but still has some texture. Stir in the lemon juice, salt and pepper.

Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Ladle tonight's portion into a bowl and top it with the yogurt, sunflower seeds and parsley. Keep the toppings for the second portion apart and add them fresh tomorrow.

This pot makes two portions. Ladle the second portion into a shallow container, let the steam off for a few minutes, and have it in the fridge within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, and reheat it once, until steaming hot (74 °C or 165 °F). It thickens overnight, so loosen it with a splash of water when you reheat it. To freeze it instead, freeze it once it is cold, thaw it in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and never refreeze it.
recipes.tip: A pinch of chili flakes in the oil wakes it up. Serve with a crunchy side salad.

recipes.name: Chicken, white bean and kale stew
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tuscan white bean soups
recipes.about: Tender chicken simmered with creamy white beans, celery, rosemary and a big handful of kale, finished with lemon. The beans and kale bring **iron, folate and calcium**, and the lemon helps your body absorb the iron.

ingredients.note: trimmed and cut into bite-size pieces

steps: Wash the kale and celery. Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces, then wash your hands, the knife and the board after the raw chicken.

Warm the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in a single layer for about 4 minutes, turning once, and dice the onion and celery meanwhile. Lift the chicken out onto a plate; it will finish cooking in the stew.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the onion and celery in the same pot until soft, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, rosemary and thyme for 1 minute.

Return the chicken to the pot with the white beans, crushed tomatoes and the broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes, and tear the kale off its stems meanwhile. The chicken should reach 74 °C (165 °F) and be tender.
Stir in the kale and simmer until it is bright and tender, about 5 minutes. Mash a few spoonfuls of beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth. Add the lemon juice, salt and pepper.

This pot makes two portions. Ladle the second portion into a shallow container, let the steam off for a few minutes, and have it in the fridge within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, and reheat it once, until steaming hot (74 °C or 165 °F). To freeze it instead, freeze it once it is cold, thaw it in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and never refreeze it.
recipes.tip: It is even better the next day. Add a splash of water when you reheat it, since the beans soak up the broth.

recipes.name: Beef and barley soup
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Eastern European beef and barley soup
recipes.about: A hearty soup of lean beef, chewy barley, carrots, celery and broccoli in a thyme-scented tomato broth. The barley thickens it as it sits, so tomorrow's bowl is even better. The beef brings **iron and zinc**, with a squeeze of lemon to lift it.
steps: Wash the carrots, celery, broccoli and parsley, and dice the onion.

Warm the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef and the onion and break the beef up with a spoon, then wash your hands after handling the raw beef. Cook, stirring now and then, until no pink remains, the onion is soft and the beef is browned in places, about 6 minutes. Dice the carrots and celery while it cooks.

Stir in the barley, carrots, celery, crushed tomatoes, broth, thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, until the barley is tender but still chewy, about 25 minutes. Cut the broccoli into small florets meanwhile. The beef should reach 71 °C (160 °F).
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the broccoli and simmer until bright green and tender, about 4 minutes. Stir in the lemon juice, salt, pepper and parsley, and add a splash of water if it is too thick.

This pot makes two portions. Cooked barley goes off quickly, so be prompt with the second portion. Ladle the second portion into a shallow container, let the steam off for a few minutes, and have it in the fridge within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, and reheat it once, until steaming hot (74 °C or 165 °F). It thickens overnight, so add water when you reheat it. To freeze it instead, freeze it once it is cold, thaw it in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and never refreeze it.
recipes.tip: Short on time? Dice the vegetables small, or use a pressure cooker: 12 minutes on high after the browning, and the barley will be ready.

recipes.name: Smoky turkey, black bean and sweet potato soup
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Cuban and Tex-Mex black bean soups
recipes.about: A thick, smoky soup of lean turkey, black beans, sweet potato and kale, with a little chili heat, lemon and fresh parsley. A spoonful of yogurt and toasted sunflower seeds finish it. The turkey and beans bring **protein, fibre and folate**, and the sweet potato adds vitamin A.

ingredients.note: peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Wash the pepper, kale, parsley and sweet potato. Dice the onion and pepper.

Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper until soft, about 6 minutes, and peel and cube the sweet potato meanwhile. Add the turkey and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains, about 5 minutes. Wash your hands after handling the raw turkey. Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, cumin and chili flakes for 1 minute.

Add the sweet potato, beans and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, until the sweet potato is tender and the turkey reaches 71 °C (160 °F), about 15 minutes. Tear the kale off its stems while it simmers.

Mash about a third of the soup against the side of the pot with a spoon, or blend a ladleful, so it turns thick and creamy. Stir in the kale and simmer until tender, about 4 minutes, then add the lemon juice and salt.
Toast the sunflower seeds in a dry pan until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Ladle the soup into bowls and top with a spoonful of yogurt, the sunflower seeds and the parsley.

This pot makes two portions. Store the soup without the toppings, and add those fresh tomorrow. Ladle the second portion into a shallow container, let the steam off for a few minutes, and have it in the fridge within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, and reheat it once, until steaming hot (74 °C or 165 °F). To freeze it instead, freeze it once it is cold, thaw it in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and never refreeze it.
recipes.tip: For less heat, leave out the chili flakes. For a thicker soup, blend more of it.

recipes.name: Salmon, potato and corn chowder
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by New England fish chowder
recipes.about: A creamy chowder of potatoes, corn and spinach with big flakes of salmon and a little parsley, thickened with the potatoes themselves instead of flour. The salmon brings **omega-3 fats and vitamin D**, and the milk brings calcium.

ingredients.note: scrubbed and cut into small cubes

steps: Wash the celery, spinach, potatoes and parsley. Dice the onion and celery.
Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and celery until soft, about 6 minutes, and cube the potatoes meanwhile. Stir in the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.

Add the potatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 12 minutes. Meanwhile, cut the salmon into bite-size chunks, then wash your hands, the knife and the board after the raw salmon. Mash about a quarter of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the chowder.
Stir in the milk and corn and heat gently until steaming, without boiling hard. Then add the salmon.
Simmer gently until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily, about 5 minutes. It should reach 70 °C (158 °F). Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then the lemon juice, salt, pepper and parsley.

This pot makes two portions. Ladle the second portion into a shallow container, let the steam off for a few minutes, and have it in the fridge within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, and reheat it once, until steaming hot (74 °C or 165 °F). Reheat it gently so the fish stays tender.
recipes.tip: Cod or haddock works if you prefer a milder fish, but then the omega-3 drops.

recipes.name: Barley minestrone with beans and greens
recipes.about: A big pot of Italian minestrone with chewy barley instead of pasta, white beans, carrot and kale in a tomato broth with a little Parmesan. A slow Saturday project that tastes even better on Sunday. The beans and barley bring **fibre and iron**, and a squeeze of lemon at the table helps.
steps: Wash the carrot, celery, mushrooms, kale and parsley. Tear the kale off its stems, slice the mushrooms and dice the carrot, celery and onion.

Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, celery and mushrooms until the mushrooms give up their water and the onion is soft, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, oregano and basil for 1 minute.
Add the barley, crushed tomatoes and broth, with a splash of water if you need it. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, until the barley is nearly tender.
Add the white beans and carrot and simmer until the barley is tender and the carrot is soft, about 12 minutes more.
Stir in the kale and simmer until it is tender, about 5 minutes. Add the salt and a splash of water if it is too thick.
Ladle tonight's portion into a bowl and top it with Parmesan and parsley. Keep the second portion plain and top it fresh tomorrow.

This pot makes two portions. Cooked barley goes off quickly, so be prompt with the second portion. Ladle the second portion into a shallow container, let the steam off for a few minutes, and have it in the fridge within 1 hour. Eat it within 3 days, and reheat it once, until steaming hot (74 °C or 165 °F). It thickens overnight, so add water when you reheat it. To freeze it instead, freeze it once it is cold, thaw it in the fridge, eat it within 2 days and never refreeze it.
recipes.tip: A squeeze of lemon or a drizzle of olive oil at the table brightens it.

recipes.name: Cod, chickpea and fennel tomato stew
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Spanish and Portuguese fish stews
recipes.about: Chunks of mild cod poached in a garlicky tomato broth with chickpeas, fennel and spinach, with smoked paprika, a pinch of chili and plenty of parsley. It comes together in about forty minutes. The cod brings **lean protein and iodine**, and the chickpeas bring fibre and folate.
steps: Wash the fennel, spinach and parsley. Slice the fennel thinly and dice the onion, then cut the cod into large chunks. Wash your hands, the knife and the board after the raw fish.
Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the fennel and onion until soft and lightly golden, about 8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika and chili flakes for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth and chickpeas. Simmer for 10 minutes so the flavours meld and the broth thickens a little.
Nestle the fish into the stew, cover, and simmer gently until it is opaque and flakes easily, about 6 minutes. It should reach 70 °C (158 °F).
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, about 1 minute. Finish with the lemon juice, salt, pepper and parsley.
Eat it the day you make it, and put anything left in a shallow container in the fridge within 2 hours. Eat it within 2 days and reheat it once, until steaming hot (74 °C or 165 °F).
recipes.tip: Haddock, pollock or any firm white fish works instead of cod.

recipes.name: Apple slices with tahini and cinnamon
recipes.about: Crisp apple slices with a spoonful of tahini to dip in and a dusting of cinnamon. Sweet, nutty and crunchy, it brings **fibre, calcium and copper**.
steps: Wash the apple, core it and cut it into slices.
Spoon the tahini into a small bowl and dust it with the cinnamon.
Dip the apple slices as you eat.

recipes.name: Cucumber and parsley salad with sunflower seeds
recipes.about: A cold, crunchy salad of cucumber, red pepper and lots of parsley with lemon and olive oil, a bright side next to a warm bowl of soup. A few sunflower seeds add **vitamin E and crunch**.
steps: Wash the cucumber, pepper and parsley. Slice the cucumber thinly and cut the pepper into thin strips.
Toss them with the lemon juice, olive oil and salt in a bowl.
Scatter the parsley and sunflower seeds on top and eat it right away, while it is crisp.
recipes.tip: Eat it beside a bowl of soup for a cool, crisp contrast.

recipes.name: Kiwi and sunflower seeds
recipes.about: Sweet-tart kiwi with a small handful of sunflower seeds. The kiwi brings **vitamin C** and the seeds bring vitamin E and magnesium.

ingredients.note: washed, halved and eaten with a spoon

steps: Wash the kiwi and cut it in half.
Eat it with a spoon, with the sunflower seeds on the side.

recipes.name: Veggie sticks with tahini lemon dip
recipes.about: Crunchy red pepper, celery and cucumber with a creamy lemony tahini dip. The tahini brings **calcium and copper**, and the pepper brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the pepper, celery and cucumber and cut them into sticks.
Stir the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt and a spoonful of water together in a small bowl until it is smooth and pourable.
Serve the sticks with the dip.

recipes.name: Apple and walnuts
recipes.about: A crisp apple with a handful of walnuts. Sweet, juicy and crunchy, it brings **fibre and a little plant omega-3**.
steps: Wash the apple and slice it.
Eat with the walnuts.

recipes.name: Crunchy spiced chickpeas
recipes.about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with cumin, smoked paprika and a squeeze of lemon. A salty, crunchy snack with **fibre, protein and folate**.

ingredients.note: drained, rinsed and patted very dry

steps: Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F). Rinse the chickpeas, then dry them really well on a clean towel.
Toss them with the oil, cumin, paprika and salt on a baking tray. Roast, shaking the tray halfway, until crisp and deep golden, about 22 minutes.
Squeeze on the lemon juice and let them cool for a few minutes to crisp up. They are best the same day.

recipes.name: Apple and fennel salad with sunflower seeds
recipes.about: Crisp apple and shaved raw fennel with lemon, olive oil and sunflower seeds, a bright, crunchy side for a warm bowl of soup. It brings **fibre, vitamin C and vitamin E**.

ingredients.note: washed, cored and cut into matchsticks

steps: Wash the apple, fennel and parsley. Cut the apple into matchsticks and shave the fennel as thinly as you can.
Toss them with the lemon juice and olive oil right away so the apple stays bright.
Scatter the sunflower seeds, parsley and black pepper over the top.

recipes.name: Greek yogurt with berries and walnuts
recipes.about: Thick Greek yogurt with berries and a few chopped walnuts. It has **protein, calcium and vitamin C** and takes a minute.
steps: Spoon the yogurt into a bowl.
Top with the berries, walnuts and cinnamon.
recipes.tip: If you are cooking for someone who is pregnant, 60 or older, 5 or under, or has a weak immune system, boil the frozen berries for 1 minute and cool them first, or use fresh.
